questions.question: World Tsunami Awareness Day is observed every year on which date?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5 November.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• World Tsunami Awareness Day is observed annually on 5 November.
 
• The day aims to raise awareness about tsunami risks and preparedness measures.
 
• It emphasises the importance of early warning systems and disaster risk reduction.
 
• The observance promotes community resilience in coastal regions.
 
• It aligns with global efforts under the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction.
 
• India actively participates in tsunami awareness and preparedness initiatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **26 December**

 
 
• This date is associated with the 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami.
 
• The tsunami caused massive loss of life in several countries, including India.
 
• It is often referenced in disaster management studies.
 
 
 
• **13 October**
 
 
• This date is observed as the International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction.
 
• It focuses on reducing exposure to natural and human-induced disasters.
 
• The day is promoted by the United Nations.
 
 
 
• **22 April**
 
 
• This date is celebrated as Earth Day globally.
 
• It focuses on environmental protection and sustainability.
 
• It is unrelated to tsunami-specific awareness.

questions.question: What is the theme of the International Day of Conscience, 2025 ?

options.text: 'To go against conscience in neither right nor safe'
'Court of conscience is the highest court'

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**‘Leave No One Behind’**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **International Day of Conscience:** The **International Day of Conscience** is observed annually on **April 5**. It was declared by the **United Nations General Assembly (UNGA)** in a resolution adopted on **July 25, 2019**, to promote a culture of peace.
 
• **Theme for 2025:** The theme for the **International Day of Conscience 2025** is **‘Leave No One Behind’**__, emphasizing inclusivity, equality, and ensuring that all individuals, regardless of background, have access to justice, human rights, and opportunities. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **‘Leave No One Behind’:** This phrase is central to the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, which aim to eliminate poverty, inequality, and injustice worldwide while safeguarding the planet. It underpins the idea of creating a more equitable and just society. *Hence, the theme aligns with global priorities.*
 
• **Other Options:** The themes ‘To go against conscience is neither right nor safe,’ ‘Court of conscience is the highest court,’ and ‘Justice, Human Rights, and Global Harmony’ are not the official themes for 2025. These phrases may reflect the principles of conscience but are not the designated theme. *Thus, these are incorrect.*
 
• **Significance of the Theme:** The theme ‘Leave No One Behind’ highlights the importance of collective responsibility and unity in addressing the challenges of poverty, inequality, and injustice on a global scale.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Details on the International Day of Conscience:**

 
 
• The **United Nations General Assembly** proclaimed the day to promote a culture of peace with love and conscience.
 
• The day calls upon individuals, communities, and nations to engage in activities that promote **peace, harmony, and inclusion.**
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• The theme ‘Leave No One Behind’ is aligned with the **2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development**, which seeks to eradicate poverty and hunger while ensuring access to education, healthcare, and opportunities for all.
 
• **Example:** SDG 10 focuses on reducing inequalities within and among countries, ensuring that marginalized and disadvantaged groups are included.
 
 
 
• **Significance of ‘Leave No One Behind’:**
 
 
• The phrase emphasizes that development and progress should be **inclusive** and benefit every individual, irrespective of their socio-economic background.
 
• **Example:** Initiatives like universal healthcare, education for all, and poverty eradication programs reflect this principle.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Relevance:**

 
 
• The theme ‘Leave No One Behind’ is especially relevant in addressing **global challenges** such as climate change, pandemics, and economic disparities.
 
• By focusing on inclusivity, the theme ensures that the benefits of development reach the most vulnerable and marginalized sections of society.
 
 
 
• **Connection to Conscience:**
 
 
• The International Day of Conscience emphasizes the role of **individual and collective conscience** in building a fair and just world.
 
• By promoting a culture of peace, the day reminds individuals of their responsibility to act with compassion, empathy, and inclusivity.

questions.question: 28th September is observed as which day?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Know Day**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• 28th September is globally observed as **International Right to Know Day**, highlighting the importance of access to information.
 
• The day was first celebrated on **28th September 2002**, established by freedom of information organizations worldwide.
 
• It emphasizes the promotion of **transparency, accountability, and the right of citizens to access public information**.
 
• The event is closely linked to the principles of democracy, ensuring active participation and informed decision-making by the public.
 
• Several countries celebrate this day to promote freedom of information acts and awareness regarding open governance practices.
 
• The day is supported by organizations like **UNESCO** and other international bodies advocating human rights and free access to information.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **De-Worming Day**

 
 
• National De-Worming Day is observed in India on **February 10** each year.
 
• This initiative aims to combat parasitic worm infections in children and adolescents aged 1-19 years.
 
• It is a flagship program under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, targeting intestinal parasitic infections that affect millions of children.
 
• The program uses Albendazole tablets as the primary method of treatment and aims to improve nutrition and overall health.
 
 
 
• **NGO Day**
 
 
• World NGO Day is observed annually on **27th February**, recognizing the contributions of non-governmental organizations globally.
 
• The day was officially recognized in 2010 by the European Union and further supported by international bodies such as the United Nations.
 
• It aims to raise awareness about the importance of NGOs in addressing social, environmental, and economic challenges worldwide.
 
• NGO Day serves as a platform for collaboration, advocacy, and acknowledgment of the role of civil society organizations.
 
 
 
• **Bicycle Day**
 
 
• World Bicycle Day is observed globally on **3rd June**, as declared by the United Nations in 2018.
 
• It aims to promote the use of bicycles as a sustainable mode of transportation for health and environmental benefits.
 
• The day encourages policymakers to prioritize cycling infrastructure and promote cycling as an affordable and eco-friendly commuting option.
 
• Bicycles are celebrated as symbols of sustainable development and accessible mobility for all, contributing to the reduction of pollution and traffic congestion.

questions.question: Who is recognized as India’s first woman teacher and co-founder of the first girls’ school in Pune?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Savitribai Phule.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **Savitribai Phule, born on 3 January 1831 in Naigaon, Maharashtra, is celebrated as India’s first woman teacher and a pioneer in women’s education.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **She co-founded the first girls’ school in Pune in 1848 alongside her husband, Jyotirao Phule.**
 
• Belonging to the Mali community, she worked against social discrimination and for the upliftment of Dalits and marginalized groups.
 
• She opposed child marriage, supported widow remarriage, and established shelters for widows and orphans.
 
• Her birth anniversary is observed as **Women’s Education Day** in Maharashtra, honoring her legacy in education and social reform.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• Savitribai Phule__

 __
 
• Recognized as India’s first woman teacher.
 
• Used education, writing, and poetry as tools for social reform and empowerment.
 
• Married to Jyotirao Phule, a leading social reformer advocating equality and anti-caste initiatives.
 
 
 
• Educational Reforms__
 __
 
• Established the first girls’ school in Pune in 1848.
 
• Worked under challenging circumstances, facing harassment and social opposition for educating girls.
 
 
 
• Social Work__
 __
 
• Advocated for Dalit upliftment, social equality, widow remarriage, and against child marriage.
 
• Established shelters for widows and orphans to provide support and protection.
 
 
 
• Legacy__
 
 
• Remembered as a symbol of women’s empowerment, social justice, and the importance of education in societal reform.
 
• Her birth anniversary, 3 January, is observed as **Women’s Education Day** in Maharashtra.

questions.question: The United Nations celebrates the International Day of the Tropics every year on which of the following day?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**29th June**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The United Nations celebrates the **International Day of the Tropics on 29th June** every year.
 
• The day was officially proclaimed by the United Nations General Assembly through a resolution adopted in 2016.
 
• The date, 29th June, was chosen to commemorate the launch of the first "State of the Tropics Report" on this day in 2014.
 
• The day aims to raise awareness about the challenges faced by tropical regions, including climate change, deforestation, biodiversity loss, and socio-economic disparities.
 
• It also highlights the unique biodiversity and cultural richness of the tropics, which are home to over 40% of the world's population and 80% of its terrestrial species.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **21st August**
 
 
• 21st August is observed as the **International Day of Remembrance and Tribute to the Victims of Terrorism**.
 
• The day is dedicated to honoring and supporting victims of terrorism and promoting their rights.
 
• It highlights the importance of solidarity with victims and survivors of terrorism worldwide.
 
 
 
• **17th July**
 
 
• 17th July is celebrated as **World Day for International Justice** or International Criminal Justice Day.
 
• It marks the anniversary of the adoption of the Rome Statute in 1998, which established the International Criminal Court (ICC).
 
• The day emphasizes the importance of combating impunity and bringing justice to those affected by crimes against humanity, genocide, and war crimes.
 
 
 
• **11th May**
 
 
• 11th May is observed as **National Technology Day in India**.
 
• It commemorates India's successful nuclear test at Pokhran in 1998, known as Operation Shakti.
 
• The day also celebrates the achievements of India's scientists, engineers, and innovators in the field of science and technology.
 
 
 
• **About the Tropics**
 
 
• The tropics refer to the region of Earth between the Tropic of Cancer (23.5° N) and the Tropic of Capricorn (23.5° S).
 
• This area experiences a warm climate year-round, with significant biodiversity and unique ecosystems.
 
• The tropics face numerous challenges, including deforestation, climate change, poverty, and health issues such as tropical diseases.
 
• Efforts to address these challenges include sustainable development programs, conservation initiatives, and international cooperation.

questions.question: What is the designated theme for **World Voice Day 2026**, which focuses on the proactive maintenance and preservation of vocal identity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Caring for Our Voices!**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **World Voice Day 2026** was observed on **April 16, 2026**, to highlight the importance of the human voice in daily communication and awareness of vocal health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The official theme for the 2026 edition is **"Caring for Our Voices!"**, which emphasizes proactive care in response to the increasing vocal demands of professionals and modern living.
 
• The theme was selected by the **Voice Committee** of the **American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery**.
 
• The initiative focuses on three core pillars: **prevention**, **hydration**, and **strain avoidance**.
 
• It encourages early intervention for voice disorders such as **spasmodic dysphonia** and seeks to increase research funding for rehabilitation.
 
• The movement uses social media hashtags like **#WVD** or **#CaringForOurVoices** to amplify its message globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History:** The event originated as **Brazilian Voice Day in 1999**, initiated by laryngologists like **Dr. Nedio Sefano** of the Brazilian Society of Laryngology and Voice.
 
• **International Expansion:** It evolved into a global phenomenon in **2002-2003** with support from the American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery.
 
• **Associated Events:** World Voice Day celebrations often associate with **National Haiku Day (April 17)** to combine health awareness with creative expression.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• World Voice Day is celebrated annually on **April 16**.
 
• The 2026 edition marks the **27th year** of this initiative, cutting across continents with professional and public participation.
 
• Primary stakeholders include **laryngologists, singers, educators,** and public speakers who are highly susceptible to voice disorders.

questions.question: In which country did Project DANTAK of the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) celebrate its 66th Raising Day on April 24, 2026?

questions.question: When is International Mind–Body Wellness Day observed annually?

questions.question: Who was the chief guest for the Republic Day Celebrations in New Delhi on 26th January 2016?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mr. Francois Hollande**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mr. Francois Hollande, the then President of France, was the Chief Guest at India's Republic Day celebrations on 26th January 2016.
 
• The invitation to Mr. Hollande was a reflection of the strong diplomatic and strategic ties between India and France.
 
• During his visit, the two countries signed several agreements, including those related to defense, nuclear energy, and space cooperation.
 
• The highlight of his visit was the announcement of the Rafale fighter jet deal, which significantly bolstered India's defense capabilities.
 
• France has consistently been a close ally of India, and Mr. Hollande's presence marked the deepened cooperation between the two nations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mr. Barack Obama**
 
 
• The then President of the United States, Mr. Barack Obama, was the Chief Guest for India's Republic Day celebrations in 2015.
 
• He became the first U.S. President to attend India's Republic Day parade as the Chief Guest.
 
• During his visit, several key agreements were finalized, including those related to civil nuclear energy and defense cooperation.
 
• His visit symbolized the strengthening strategic partnership between India and the U.S.
 
 
 
• **Mr. Shinzo Abe**
 
 
• The then Prime Minister of Japan, Mr. Shinzo Abe, was the Chief Guest at India's Republic Day celebrations in 2014.
 
• His visit emphasized the strong economic and cultural ties between India and Japan.
 
• Japan has been a key development partner for India, particularly in infrastructure projects such as the Delhi Metro and the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project.
 
 
 
• **Ms. Angela Merkel**
 
 
• Ms. Angela Merkel, the then Chancellor of Germany, has not been a Chief Guest at India's Republic Day celebrations.
 
• However, Germany and India share a strong bilateral relationship, especially in areas like trade, technology, and climate change.
 
 
 
• **Republic Day Celebrations**
 
 
• India's Republic Day is celebrated on 26th January every year to honor the day the Constitution of India came into effect in 1950.
 
• The Chief Guest at the Republic Day celebrations is usually a head of state or government from a foreign nation, signifying India's diplomatic outreach and relationships.
 
• The parade held in New Delhi showcases India's cultural diversity, military strength, and technological advancements.
 
 
</ul

The theme for the 18th edition in 2026 is "Viksit Bharat: Citizen-Centric Governance and Development at the Last Mile".
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel originally addressed the civil servants and called them the "steel frame of India" at Vigyan Bhawan.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel originally addressed the civil servants and called them the "steel frame of India" at Vigyan Bhawan.**__

• The **theme** for the 18th edition in 2026 is "**Viksit Bharat: Citizen-Centric Governance and Development at the Last Mile**", making the related statement correct.

• The **Prime Minister’s Awards for Excellence in Public Administration** are presented to honor outstanding public service and groundbreaking initiatives.

questions.question: When is World Pangolin Day observed annually to raise awareness about the illegal trade and conservation of pangolins?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Third Saturday of February.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **World Pangolin Day 2026 highlighted the complex and shifting illegal global trade routes involving pangolins, as reported by CITES.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **World Pangolin Day is observed annually on the third Saturday of February.**
 
• **The day aims to raise awareness about pangolin conservation and the threats posed by illegal wildlife trade.**
 
• **The 2026 Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) report identified 74 countries involved in illegal pangolin trade across 178 unique routes.**
 
• **A significant 67 per cent of high-volume trade routes were used only once, indicating traffickers frequently change routes to evade detection.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pangolin**__

 __
 
• Pangolins are scaly mammals found in Asia and Africa.
 
• They are considered the most trafficked mammals in the world.
 
• All eight species are listed under Appendix I of CITES, prohibiting international commercial trade.
 
 
 
• **CITES**__
 __
 
• Full form: Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora.
 
• An international agreement between governments to ensure that trade in wild animals and plants does not threaten their survival.
 
• Established in 1975.
 
 
 
• **Whole Pangolin Equivalent**__
 
 
• A measurement unit used to estimate the number of individual pangolins represented in seized scales or products.
 
• Helps standardise reporting of wildlife seizures across countries.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding International Labour Day:

I. It is observed annually on 2nd May.

II. Its theme for the year 2026 is ‘Ensuring a Healthy Psychosocial Working Environment’.

Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The world observes **May 1** as **International Labour Day** to commemorate the contributions of the working class and raise awareness about labour rights, fair wages, and safe working conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement I is incorrect:** The **International Labour Organization (ILO)** is observed annually on **1st May.**
 
• **Statement II is correct:** Its **theme **for the year 2026 is ‘Ensuring a Healthy Psychosocial Working Environment’.
 
• By the late 19th century, **Chicago’s national convention by the American Federation of Labour** announced a legal working time of **eight hours**. Following this, over **160 countries** adopted the eight-hour working policy globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• On **May 1, 1886**, the **Marxist International Socialist Congress** passed a resolution calling for a large peaceful strike at the **Haymarket Affair in Chicago**, demanding proper wages, paid leave, and an eight-hour daily limit.
 
• The peaceful protest eventually turned violent due to bomb-throwing, leading to the deaths of **seven officers and at least four civilians**. This incident cemented **May 1** as a day of international solidarity for workers' rights.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• Also known as **May Day**, the observance gives workers a platform to urge policymakers to fight for social fairness.
 
• **India** observes a **national holiday** on **May 1**, marking the occasion with parades, speeches, rallies, and cultural events highlighting the Indian labour movement.

questions.question: What is the theme of World Earth Day 2026?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Our Power, Our Planet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **World Earth Day 2026** is observed to raise awareness about environmental protection, highlighting issues like climate change and biodiversity loss.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The official theme for **World Earth Day 2026** is **"Our Power, Our Planet"**.
 
• This theme places strong emphasis on leveraging **community action** and accelerating the global transition to **renewable energy**.
 
• It aims to boost accountability for environmental damage to effectively tackle the ongoing **climate crisis**.
 
• The theme underscores that collective, daily actions from individuals are crucial in achieving a **sustainable future**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Origins:** Earth Day was first celebrated on **April 22, 1970**.
 
• **Initiator:** The movement was spearheaded by **Gaylord Nelson**, a U.S. senator who was deeply moved by the devastating impact of a massive oil spill.
 
• **Global Participation:** What started as a national movement in the United States has now grown globally, with over **190 countries** participating in sustainability efforts.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

questions.question: When is National Engineer's Day observed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15 September**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• National Engineer's Day is observed every year on **15 September** in India.
 
• The day commemorates the birth anniversary of **Sir Mokshagundam Visvesvaraya**, a renowned engineer and Bharat Ratna awardee.
 
• Sir M. Visvesvaraya is known for his outstanding contributions in the field of engineering and his role in the construction of dams, irrigation systems, and flood control mechanisms in India.
 
• The day serves to recognize the contributions of engineers in nation-building and to inspire young minds to pursue careers in engineering and technology.
 
• National Engineer's Day is celebrated with events such as technical seminars, workshops, and discussions in engineering institutions across the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **10 December:**

 
 
• This day is observed as **Human Rights Day** globally, commemorating the adoption of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) by the United Nations General Assembly in 1948.
 
• The day highlights the importance of human rights and promotes equality, justice, and human dignity.
 
 
 
• **14 April:**
 
 
• 14 April is celebrated as **Ambedkar Jayanti**, marking the birth anniversary of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the chief architect of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The day is also observed to promote social justice and equality, as Dr. Ambedkar was a staunch advocate of marginalized communities' rights.
 
 
 
• **1 October:**
 
 
• 1 October is globally observed as **International Day of Older Persons**, as designated by the United Nations in 1990.
 
• The day aims to raise awareness about issues affecting older adults, such as elder abuse and healthcare, and to appreciate their contributions to society.

questions.question: The "International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer" (World Ozone Day) is observed annually on which date to commemorate the signing of the Montreal Protocol?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**September 16**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer** is observed globally on **September 16** every year to commemorate the signing of the **Montreal Protocol**.
 
• The **Montreal Protocol** on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer was signed on **September 16, 1987**, and is widely regarded as one of the most successful environmental agreements in history.
 
• In **1994**, the **United Nations General Assembly** (UNGA) officially proclaimed this date to raise awareness about the **Ozone Layer** and the scientific and political efforts required to protect it.
 
• The **Ozone Layer** is a region of Earth's **stratosphere** that contains high concentrations of ozone (O3) and acts as a shield, absorbing about 97 to 99 percent of the Sun's medium-frequency **ultraviolet (UV) radiation**.
 
• The primary objective of the day is to promote the phasing out of **Ozone-Depleting Substances** (ODS), such as **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)**, **Halons**, and **Carbon tetrachloride**, which cause the thinning of the ozone layer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **September 5**:
 
 
• This date is celebrated as **Teachers' Day** in India to honor **Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan**, the second President of India and a renowned philosopher.
 
• Internationally, it is recognized as the **International Day of Charity**, established by the UN to commemorate the passing of **Mother Teresa**.
 
 
 
• **October 16**:
 
 
• Observed as **World Food Day** to mark the founding of the **Food and Agriculture Organization** (FAO) of the United Nations in **1945**.
 
 
 
• **December 11**:
 
 
• Designated as **International Mountain Day** by the UN to promote sustainable development in mountain regions.
 
• It is also observed as **UNICEF Day**, marking the creation of the **United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund** on this day in **1946**.

questions.question: Which initiative was promoted by Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan on World Environment Day 2025?

options.text: Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam 2.0 tree drive

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam 2.0 tree drive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **World Environment Day 2025**, the Education Minister of India, **Dharmendra Pradhan**, promoted the **‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam 2.0 tree drive’**. This initiative was aimed at encouraging individuals and communities to plant trees in honor of their mothers.
 
• The campaign is a continuation of the earlier **‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’** initiative, which was launched to create environmental awareness and promote tree plantation as a tribute to mothers. The updated version, **2.0**, expanded its scope and outreach significantly.
 
• The initiative aligns with the goals of sustainable development and emphasizes the importance of community participation in tackling **environmental degradation**. It calls for individuals to plant a tree and nurture it as a lifelong commitment, symbolizing a bond of care and responsibility similar to that shared with one’s mother.
 
• This program was launched in collaboration with schools, colleges, and community organizations to maximize awareness about **climate change** and the need for afforestation. Students and youth were the primary target audiences to ensure long-term engagement with environmental conservation.
 
• The initiative also included educational workshops, tree-planting drives, and campaigns to sensitize people about the importance of biodiversity and green cover. It encouraged the plantation of **native tree species** that contribute to local ecosystems and support wildlife.
 
• The campaign gained significant traction on social media platforms, with the use of hashtags such as **#EkPedMaaKeNaam**. This helped in promoting the initiative to a wider audience and involving urban as well as rural communities. 
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam 2.0 tree drive.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Background of World Environment Day:**

 
 
• **World Environment Day** is celebrated on **June 5th** annually and is one of the most notable global platforms for raising awareness about environmental issues.
 
• The day is led by the **United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)**, and each year focuses on a specific theme. The theme for 2025 focused on **“Restoring Ecosystems”**, which aligned with the goals of the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam 2.0’ initiative.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Tree Plantation:**
 
 
• Tree plantation drives play a vital role in combating **climate change**, reducing air pollution, and improving biodiversity. They contribute to carbon sequestration, which is crucial for maintaining ecological balance.
 
• Planting native trees helps restore **local ecosystems** by providing habitat and food for wildlife, improving soil health, and preventing erosion.
 
• **Example:** Countries like **India, China, and Ethiopia** have implemented large-scale afforestation programs to address the challenges of deforestation and desertification.
 
 
 
• **Details of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Plastic-Free India Campaign:** This campaign focuses on reducing single-use plastics and promoting sustainable alternatives. While important, it is unrelated to the **tree plantation initiative** promoted by Dharmendra Pradhan on World Environment Day 2025.
 
• **Clean Ganga Youth Initiative:** This initiative is aimed at cleaning and rejuvenating the **Ganga river** and involves youth participation. It is not directly related to tree plantation.
 
• **National Coastal Clean-up Mission:** This initiative focuses on cleaning beaches and coastal areas to address marine pollution. It is unrelated to the **‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam 2.0 tree drive’**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Benefits of Tree Plantation:**

 
 
• Trees act as **carbon sinks**, absorbing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and mitigating the impacts of global warming.
 
• They improve **air quality** by filtering pollutants and releasing oxygen, contributing to better public health outcomes.
 
• Tree plantation supports **biodiversity conservation** by creating habitats for birds, insects, and other wildlife.
 
 
 
• **Policy Support for Afforestation:**
 
 
• **India’s National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)** includes measures like the **National Mission for a Green India** to enhance forest cover and ecosystem services.
 
• **Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)** initiatives also support afforestation efforts, with companies funding tree-planting programs under environmental sustainability goals.

questions.question: Vishanu Sankraman Pratirodh Abhyas was conducted to assess India’s preparedness for which of the following?
questions.solution:
The Correct Option is Zoonotic disease outbreaks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• A large-scale multi-sector mock exercise titled **Vishanu Sankraman Pratirodh Abhyas** was conducted in **Khandwa District, Madhya Pradesh from 2nd to 5th November, 2025** to assess **India’s preparedness for zoonotic disease outbreaks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• The simulation modeled a **Crimean-Congo Haemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) **outbreak in humans and livestock to evaluate real-time investigation, pathogen detection, containment strategies, and inter-agency coordination.
 
• Key stakeholders involved in the exercise included the **National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC)**, the **Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR),** the High Security Animal Disease Laboratory (HSADL), Bhopal, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), and the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying (DAHD), among others.
 
• The drill strengthened** India’s One Health approach **by underscoring the interlinkages between human, animal, and ecosystem health, while enhancing integrated disease-control systems and pandemic preparedness.

questions.question: The Lokpal of India observed its foundation day on 16 January 2026. Which of the following statements regarding the Lokpal of India is ***incorrect***?

options.text: Lokpal was established after the coming into force of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, on 16 January 2014.
Lokpal consists of a Chairperson and eight members, including four Judicial and four Non-Judicial members.
Lokpal has the mandate to inquire into corruption allegations against the Prime Minister, Union Ministers and Members of Parliament.
Lokpal directly conducts suo-moto criminal trials and awards punishments in corruption cases.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lokpal directly conducts criminal trials and awards punishments in corruption cases.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Lokpal of India observed its Foundation Day on 16 January, marking its establishment under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Lokpal was established on 16 January 2014 after Section 3 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 came into force.**
 
• It consists of a Chairperson and eight Members, including four Judicial and four Non-Judicial members.
 
• Its jurisdiction covers corruption complaints against the Prime Minister, Union Ministers, Members of Parliament and central government officials.
 
• Lokpal does not conduct criminal trials or award punishments; it inquires into complaints and can direct investigative agencies such as the CBI.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Lokpal of India__

 __
 
• A statutory anti-corruption body at the Union level.
 
• Functions as an independent ombudsman to ensure accountability in public life.
 
 
 
• Appointment Process__
 __
 
• Members are appointed by the President of India.
 
• Appointments are based on recommendations of a Selection Committee under Section 4 of the Act.
 
 
 
• Powers of Lokpal__
 __
 
• Can order preliminary inquiries and investigations.
 
• May refer cases to agencies like the CBI but does not act as a trial court.
 
 
 
• Objective__
 
 
• To promote integrity, transparency and accountability in governance.
 
• To strengthen public trust in democratic institutions.
